source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Obtain and review existing maintenance records for the bridge. These records will provide a history of previous issues, repairs, and inspections. Document this information, including dates and details of past maintenance activities, materials used, and the personnel involved. This historical data will provide insight into the structural changes and potential ongoing issues with the bridge.

3. Conduct a thorough visual inspection.
Ensure a comprehensive visual inspection is conducted on every aspect of the bridge structure. Check all accessible components such as deck, superstructure (beams and girders), substructure (abutments and piers), bearings, expansion joints, and railings. Record detailed descriptions, including their condition, any observed defects (such as cracks, spalling, corrosion, or settlement), and the severity of these defects.

4. Use non-destructive testing (NDT) methods.
Implement NDT methods such as ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle inspection, and ground-penetrating radar to identify
